quickStart.item_06: For a police emergency in Japan call 110; for fire or ambulance call 119.
quickStart.item_16: For medical care, bring your registered My Number Card health insurance certificate or the eligibility confirmation document issued by your insurer, as applicable.
quickStart.item_59: Review emergency contacts, health information, legal document locations, insurance, banks, investments, pensions, and essential liabilities.
quickStart.item_29: If someone has died, contact the municipal office, Japan Pension Service, financial institutions, insurers, and tax office as relevant; requirements depend on the case.
quickStart.item_41: Keep the export encrypted. Never put My Number Card PINs, e-Tax credentials, passwords, authentication codes, or recovery keys in it.

legalNotes.item_51: My Number is a 12-digit identifier assigned to people with a residence record in Japan. The Individual Number Card is a separate card; My Number itself is sensitive personal information.
legalNotes.item_111: Since December 2024, new health insurance certificates are no longer issued. Existing certificates remained valid until their expiry, up to December 1, 2025; registered My Number Cards or insurer-issued eligibility certificates are used under current arrangements. Confirm with the insurer.
legalNotes.item_43: Japan's National Pension and Employees' Pension Insurance have different enrolment and benefits rules. Survivor benefits depend on contribution records and eligibility.
legalNotes.item_39: Inheritance tax may apply depending on the estate, residence, citizenship, and other circumstances. The National Tax Agency publishes current thresholds and filing rules; do not rely on static amounts in this organizer.
legalNotes.item_03: Adult guardianship, voluntary guardianship, wills, and private powers of attorney are distinct legal mechanisms. Confirm formal requirements with the Family Court, a notary, or a qualified Japanese lawyer.
legalNotes.item_21: Emergency numbers: Japan National Tourism Organization: https://www.japan.travel/en/plan/emergencies/

recoveryRoadmap.description: A general checklist after a death in Japan. Confirm the representative's authority and current municipal, pension, court, and tax requirements before acting.

meta.title: Family Recovery Roadmap - Japan
meta.reviewedBy: Government sources reviewed; case-specific legal and tax advice may be needed

intro.condolence: We are sorry for your loss. This checklist is intended to make the first practical steps clearer.
intro.howToUse: Follow municipal death-registration instructions, identify the executor or representative, notify relevant insurers and providers, and keep a record of each action.

startHere.0: Follow the municipal death-registration and residence-card procedures that apply to the circumstances.
startHere.1: Locate the will and identify the executor; seek legal advice if there is no will or the estate is complex.
startHere.2: Contact the health insurer, Japan Pension Service, banks, employer, insurers, and tax office as appropriate.
startHere.3: List assets, debts, regular payments, and claims; confirm authority and obligations before changing payments or distributing property.
startHere.4: Keep a log of contacts, forms, and documents supplied. Never use the deceased person's My Number Card PIN or online credentials.

legalFramework.2: National Tax Agency inheritance-tax and final income-tax rules.
legalFramework.3: Family Court adult guardianship procedures and relevant notarial instruments.
legalFramework.4: Bank, insurer, property, and investment provider processes.
